{"parentUuid":"8a953821-bf01-4e3b-974e-f00337ba762f","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMYzwRbGUVAF7R9H9h1N","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The check flags the admin templates, but the rubric only cares about the published site. The check script scans more than the rubric asks for. I changed no files.\n\n## What the check scans\n\nIt lives in `scripts/check_submission.py`, in `git_state()`:\n\n```python\nsh(\"git\", \"grep\", \"-l\", \"-e\", 'href=\"/', \"-e\", 'src=\"/', \"--\", \"*.html\")\n```\n\n- It scans every **git-tracked** file matching `*.html`, at any depth.\n- That means `templates/**` in the source repo, not `site/` (gitignored, never tracked) and not the `gh-pages` branch.\n- Today it matches 9 files, all under `templates/admin/`. There are 14 hits: `/admin/...` links, the `Cancel` links, and the recap image preview `src=\"/admin/recaps/{id}/images/...\"`.\n- The public templates in `templates/public/` don't match.\n- It runs at stage 1 and stage 2, so it shows as a FAIL on either.\n\n## What the rubric says\n\n- **S1.7:** \"zero root-absolute paths in `gh-pages`\".\n- **F2:** \"zero root-absolute paths **on the published site**\".\n- **T6:** the grader greps the `gh-pages` branch for `href=\"/` and `src=\"/`.\n\nAll three name the published output. The admin console never goes on the public internet (`CLAUDE.md`, ADR-001). Root-absolute paths break on a GitHub Pages project subfolder, and the admin console is never served from one. For the admin console they are correct, since it is always served from `/`.\n\nSo the intent is only the published `site/` output. The script's check is broader than that. I'd call it a check bug, not a real violation.\n\nThe check you didn't ask about is `test_published_html_uses_relative_paths`, plus the T05 and T07 tests. These render the actual output and look for `href=\"/` and `src=\"/`. They are the correct form of this rule and are green.\n\n## Options\n\n| Option | Cost |\n|---|---|\n| **1. Leave as is** | Free. But `check_submission.py` reports a permanent FAIL for a non-violation. You'd need to explain it in the report. The grader runs this script first, so it's a bad first impression. It might also be counted against you if the rubric's judge reads the script's output literally. |\n| **2. Exclude the admin templates in the check** | One-line pathspec change, e.g. `\":(exclude)templates/admin\"`, or scan only `templates/public` and `site/`. Matches the rubric's intent. Cost: it edits the instructor's script, which is part of the template and \"the judge runs this first\". The grader may run their own copy, so it might not help at all. It could also look like gaming the check, so I'd tell the instructor first. |\n| **3. Make admin paths relative** | Highest cost and wrong direction. About 14 edits, and relative paths across `/admin`, `/admin/recaps/3`, and `/admin/recaps/3/images/x` vary by depth. Every redirect and `formaction` would need reworking, and the 497-test suite asserts many of these paths. It adds bug risk for no rubric benefit, since the admin console is never published. |\n\n## Recommendation\n\nI'd use option 2, plus a short note to the instructor, because their script is the thing that is wrong. If you can't change the script in your submission, use option 1 and put a line in the report saying the 14 hits are all admin-console templates that are never published, and that the output tests prove `site/` is clean.\n\nI'd avoid option 3.\n\nTell me which one you want and I'll make the change."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1469,"cache_read_input_tokens":141137,"output_tokens":1160,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1469,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1160,"cache_read_input_tokens":141137,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1469,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1469},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"e27a8fb2-e08f-46de-a316-108a4d7302a5","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CgMYzw6kYBskT6Kvfimt4","requestRef":"0109b729-554b-4c0a-b340-eaa94336c727","requestedModel":"claude-sonnet-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"88601f27-927a-4ea1-bdf2-16ea7cdc1d6a","timestamp":"2026-10-24T18:41:32.985Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"504ad17f-7c8b-4d9d-8463-7be256b0fa6a","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"2f9c547a-bc89-4034-8724-473eb17d3f6b","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"3ff0dcaf-e5c6-4c23-8200-c51f0a2acba6","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: the uncommitted T09 changes. Focus on: cms backup (path handling, symlinks, refusing folders inside the repo, no secrets or .env in the archive, the SQLite copy is consistent, overwrite behaviour); the seed script (idempotency, no real passwords or secrets in code or history, .env.example contents, behaviour with missing variables); cms publish refusal handling (exit code, no partial site/, message does not leak paths or secrets); whether the final route audit really covers every Admin-only route with an Editor 403 row and no skips; CSRF on every POST form; the changed assertions in test_t00 and test_t01 (did anything get weakened); and the gitignore additions. Report findings only, do not change any files."}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"be22b511-8be5-46db-8246-04c74b5c710d","timestamp":"2026-10-24T18:44:38.833Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"504ad17f-7c8b-4d9d-8463-7be256b0fa6a","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

I ran probes only in /private/tmp and did not run pytest. I found no HARD violations of a documented standard. The archive holds no .env or key files, and password hashes in the DB are expected.\n  \n  1. BUG, app/cli.py:35. A missing database file is silently \"backed up\".\n     - `sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)` creates a 0-byte file when none exists (probed). Backup then exits 0 with an archive holding an empty DB, and leaves a stray empty `cms.db` at DATABASE_PATH.\n     - Failing scenario: `CMS_DATABASE` is mistyped, or the command runs before the first `serve`. The user believes they have a backup.\n     - Fix: check `DATABASE_PATH.is_file()` first, or open with `file:...?mode=ro` URI.\n  \n  2. BUG, app/cli.py:28. The \"inside the repo\" check can be bypassed on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS).\n     - `Path('/Users/andrewv/Code/iphs400-mp2-cms/newdir').resolve()` keeps the wrong case for a path that does not exist yet (probed). So `ROOT.resolve() in target.parents` is False and the archive lands in the repo.\n     - Failing scenario: `cms backup ~/Code/iphs400-mp2-cms/backups`. The archive is gitignored by name, but a differently named folder is not covered.\n     - Fix: compare with `os.path.normcase`/`samefile` on the nearest existing ancestor, or compare `os.path.realpath(...).lower()`.\n     - A relative path, `..`, and a symlinked repo root are fine. `settings.ROOT` is already resolved, and the test's symlink case works.\n  \n  3. BUG, app/cli.py:32-49. Writing the archive is not safe.\n     - The mode is \"w\", so a second run in the same minute silently overwrites the first archive.\n     - A failure partway (for example a `FileNotFoundError` on a file deleted between `rglob` and `write`, or a read error) leaves a truncated, valid-looking `cms-backup-*.zip`. Only the temp DB copy is cleaned up.\n     - Fix: write to `.part` and rename, and use mode \"x\" or add seconds to the name.\n  \n  4. BUG, app/cli.py:45-48. Uploads symlinks are followed. `path.is_file()` and `z.write` follow a symlink, so `uploads/x.png -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa` puts the key in the archive. Skip `path.is_symlink()` or verify `path.resolve()` is under `UPLOADS.resolve()`. Zip entry names are fine: POSIX relative with no `..`.\n  \n  5. BUG, app/cli.py:72-77. `cms publish` leaks an absolute path.\n     - app/publish.py:77-78 puts `settings.UPLOADS` (absolute) in the refusal message, and the CLI prints it verbatim (`/Users/andrewv/...`). No secrets are leaked.\n     - Exit code is 1 and `site/` is untouched, because both checks run before the `rmtree` at publish.py:114.\n     - Other exceptions still traceback, for example a rendering error after the rmtree leaves a partial `site/`. That is pre-existing, outside the diff.\n  \n  6. BUG, app/seed.py:41-66. `seed_content` is idempotent only on the complete path.\n     - The early return keys on the Trip slug, and the writes are not in one transaction.\n     - If a Recap or Page fails after `create_trip` (a slug clash with user data, for example), every re-run returns early and the content stays half-seeded.\n     - Fix: key the check on the last item created, or run it all in one transaction.\n     - `ids[EDITOR_EMAIL]` raises KeyError if the accounts were renamed or deactivated.\n  \n  7. BUG (minor), scripts/seed_demo.py:24. A whitespace-only password (`\"   \"`) passes `not admin_pw` and gets hashed as a real password. The tests cover only unset and `\"\"`. Use `.strip()`.\n  \n  8. JUDGEMENT, tests/test_t09.py:270-275. The `finally` block of `test_backup_inside_the_repository_is_refused` runs `unlink()` on every `ROOT/cms-backup-*.zip` and `ROOT/docs/cms-backup-*.zip`. That includes real backups the owner left there, not just ones the test made. Record the pre-existing set, or only delete files created after the test started. The `rmtree` targets are probe-named subfolders, which is fine.\n  \n  9. JUDGEMENT, tests/test_t09.py:278-284. The symlink test asserts only that nothing was written. It does not assert the message, so a crash would pass it. The test also writes under the real `ROOT/docs` if the implementation is wrong.\n  \n  10. JUDGEMENT, app/seed.py:25-30. The fourth tuple field of `DEMO_RECAPS`/`DEMO_PAGES`, the \"owner role\" comment and the `\"editor\"` value, is never read (`_` at line 52). `DEMO_PAGES` positions are used. This is speculative generality or a mysterious field. The seed also repeats the transition logic that `recaps.transition` already owns.\n  \n  11. JUDGEMENT, tests/test_t01.py:43-46. The `{other}` rows are ownership rows, not admin-only routes, but they sit in `ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES`. They are real: an Admin-owned Draft is created per row, and the 403 plus unchanged-row assertion is genuine.\n     - Tightening to `==403` is a strengthening.\n     - A fresh DB per test means no slug clashes. Cost is two extra requests per row.\n     - The old \"hello admin\" and the new `<h1>Dashboard</h1>` assertions are equivalent in strength.\n  \n  12. JUDGEMENT, tests/test_t09.py:188-205. The refusal test does not check that the message omits the absolute uploads path (see 5), so it would not catch the leak.\n  \n  Fine, no action:\n  - .gitignore: `cms-backup-*.zip` has no slash, so it matches at any depth. Other archive extensions and the output folder are not covered, but backups go outside the repo anyway.\n  - `.env.example` contains only placeholders. A `git log -S` probe for `[REDACTED-CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD]` finds only the initial commit.\n  - Source and destination SQLite connections are closed in `finally`. `backup()` is WAL-safe.\n  - No minute-rollover flake: the tests make a single backup call and match the name by regex.\n  - Seed subprocess env hygiene is good: CMS_* vars are stripped, and DB and uploads are in tmp_path.\n</agent-message>"}

A mistyped `CMS_DATABASE` would trigger this.\n2. `app/cli.py:28` — the \"inside the repo\" check can be bypassed on macOS's case-insensitive filesystem. `~/Code/iphs400-mp2-cms/newdir` doesn't resolve to the repo's case when the folder doesn't exist yet, so the archive lands inside the repo. Relative paths, `..`, and the symlink case are fine.\n3. `app/cli.py:32-49` — the archive is not written safely. A second backup in the same minute silently overwrites the first, and a failure partway leaves a truncated, valid-looking zip.\n4. `app/cli.py:45-48` — symlinks inside `uploads/` are followed, so `uploads/x.png -> ~/.ssh/id_rsa` would put a private key in the archive.\n5. `app/cli.py:72-77` — a refusal for a missing image file prints the absolute `UPLOADS` path.
